title: The Caravan Finds No Refuge in the Village

blocks.text: Seeking a moment of shelter, the battered caravan turns toward a nearby village, but the inhabitants shut their doors and refuse entry. Those who hide in stacks or enclosures are discovered, plundered, and in some cases burned alive, making the page one of the bleakest scenes in the whole Ghallughara sequence.

Charat Singh returns to the defense in anger and keeps up such steady fire that loaders must keep handing him fresh muskets. His intervention wins a brief breathing space, especially when Abdali's line momentarily pauses for water and the caravan can be drawn together again.

In that interval The Singhs guarded the caravan from both the flanks, enclosing the survivors as protectively as they could. The page emphasizes that the Khalsa could not rely on local refuge and had to become its own moving wall of defense.
